final_candidates.decision_summary: Strongest all-around candidate: high escape (0.887) with the best PLM plausibility (0.657) and best structure compatibility (0.984). Charge-introducing substitution in an antigenic head region balancing escape and fitness.

Highest escape score (0.964) with moderate PLM plausibility (0.378); structure score not applicable for this position. A classic H1 Sa-antigenic-site charge-reversal mechanism with acceptable viability signals.
Very high escape (0.901) and excellent structure compatibility (0.973), but low PLM (0.029) and zero MSA frequency indicate fitness risk. Retained as rank 3 on strong escape/structure support.

stop_reason.detail: Evidence is sufficient across phenotype, PLM, and structure dimensions for the top candidates; remaining gaps (K157E structure N/A) cannot be resolved by further tool calls.

history.rationale: Mature HA1 residue 159 in the Sa antigenic site; charge-flip substitutions at this exposed loop are classic H1 antibody-escape changes while preserving the fold.

Lysine-to-glutamate at a solvent-exposed antigenic-site residue is a classic charge-reversal escape mechanism; plausible as both escape and viability-neutral. No evidence collected yet, so confidence stays at prior.
High escape (0.901) with excellent structure compatibility (0.973); low PLM plausibility slightly tempers confidence but structure is the stronger replication proxy.
Very high structure compatibility (0.973) and good escape (0.901), but PLM (0.029) and MSA frequency (0.000) both flag fitness risk. Demoted below K157E and Q205K.
Mature HA1 193 near the Sb/190-helix antigenic surface; Asn-to-Asp here alters an epitope contact with modest structural cost.
Conservative N-to-D substitution near an N-linked-glycosylation-adjacent antigenic region; retains size while altering local chemistry. Awaiting evidence.
Moderate escape (0.764) with good structure (0.931); retained but ranked below the leaders.
Moderate escape (0.764) and good structure, but near-zero PLM and zero MSA frequency make it a poor trade; rank 5.
Mature HA1 145 on the Ca/RBS-periphery antigenic ridge; removing a charged Arg disrupts antibody binding without touching the receptor-binding pocket core.
Removal of a charged arginine in a surface loop can disrupt antibody contact; may carry some fitness cost, hence mid confidence.
PLM plausibility is essentially zero (0.005), strongly suggesting a non-viable substitution despite decent escape/structure.

rejection.reason: PLM plausibility is essentially zero (0.005), strongly suggesting a non-viable substitution despite decent escape/structure.

history.rationale: Mature HA1 154 at the Sa/Ca boundary; introducing Asp adds negative charge on an antigenic loop, a common escape strategy.
Loop-localized glycine-to-aspartate could alter local conformation and escape, but glycine loss in loops can be structurally risky. Needs structure_compatibility check.
High escape (0.942) with acceptable structure (0.850) but weak PLM (0.116); kept as backup.
High escape (0.942) and decent structure (0.850), but low PLM (0.116) and low MSA support (0.030) suggest a fitness cost; retained as backup, rank 4.
Mature HA1 188 in the Sb antigenic site; surface charge change expected to reduce antibody recognition with limited folding impact.
Charge-introducing substitution in antigenic site region; moderate prior, needs evidence.
Balanced profile: escape 0.888, best PLM score (0.657), best structure score (0.984) — best combined escape-with-fitness candidate.

Q205K is the only candidate with consistently strong evidence across all four dimensions: high escape (0.887), best PLM plausibility (0.657), best structure compatibility (0.984), and the highest MSA mutant frequency among charge/receptor-distal candidates (0.041). Confirmed as rank 1.
Mature HA1 156 in the Sa head loop; a modest polar substitution at a variable antigenic position with some glycosylation-shield potential.
Serine-to-asparagine is conservative and could modulate glycosylation/antibody binding; weak-moderate prior.
Lowest escape (0.743) and low PLM (0.021); deprioritized.
Best MSA tolerance (0.065) and good structure, but lowest escape (0.743) and weak PLM; retained only as low-priority diversity option, rank 6.
Mature HA1 227 in the 220-loop near the receptor-binding site; a conservative polar change on an antigenically exposed residue, with some receptor-proximity fitness risk.
WT residue at position 244 in the provided sequence is Y, not N, so N244D is inconsistent with the numbering requirement and is removed.

history.rationale: Verified WT residue at 157 is K in the given sequence; a charge-reversal in the Sa/Sb head region is a well-known H1 escape mechanism class. Added as a diversity-expanding candidate for the antigenic head surface.
Highest escape score (0.964) and the best PLM among charge-reversal candidates, but structure evidence is not applicable (WT mismatch at mapped residue), leaving fitness uncertain.

Highest escape score (0.964) with moderate PLM plausibility (0.378) and a natural E-at-157 frequency of 0.006 indicating evolutionary tolerance is weak but nonzero; structure score unavailable for this position. Promoted to rank 2 on escape strength plus tolerable plausibility.
